analysis: Reviewed two base_text excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 44943-46535). They contain only repetitive token-ID arrays, a synthetic 'long_prompt' vector (repeated 'cache' text, scope_id 'fixture-scope', date 2028-02-29), and plan/chain-hash data. No secrets, credentials, real consumer prompts, keys, or executable code are present. The patch excerpt (truncated) shows the PR regenerating fixture vectors: adds additional_context {enable_thinking:false} to template input, and changes prompt_token_count and block-boundary chain hashes (e.g. 803 -> 767 tokens). This is a test-fixture data change with no runtime authorization, attestation, encryption, or WebSocket behavior. The only security relevance is indirect: prompt-contract IDs, token counts, and chain hashes feed prefix-cache keying (T-041, A-001). A mismatch between provider and coordinator/platform expectations of these vectors could cause cache-key or contract divergence, but that is a correctness/availability matter and cannot be verified from the supplied evidence. Only the base side of the later hunks was supplied, so the head values are not directly verifiable. Open integration question: whether the Swift prompt-contract implementation and the platform-owned consumer of these vectors changed consistently with the enable_thinking: false context. No concrete security regression identified.
